We will be using data from the article: Curtis et al., 2012, Genomic and Transcriptomic Architecture of Breast Tumor. / Estaremos usando datos del artículo: Curtis et al., 2012, Genomic and Transcriptomic Architecture of Breast Tumor.

I am giving you the initial code, the basics to start building a ggplot of Tumor Size vs Type of Breast Surgery. / Les estoy dando el inicial, lo básico para construir un ggplot de Tumor Size vs Type of Breast Surgery.

Be sure to follow R syntax carefully and include all plots requested in the assignment. / Sigan cuidadosamente la sintaxis de R e incluyan todos los gráficos solicitados en la asignación.

Load libraries

library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(janitor)
## 
## Attaching package: 'janitor'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     chisq.test, fisher.test

Load data metabric <- read.csv(“brca_metabric_clinical_data.csv”) %>% clean_names() head(metabric[, 1:5]) ## study_id patient_id sample_id age_at_diagnosis type_of_breast_surgery ## 1 brca_metabric MB-0000 MB-0000 75.65 MASTECTOMY ## 2 brca_metabric MB-0002 MB-0002 43.19 BREAST CONSERVING ## 3 brca_metabric MB-0005 MB-0005 48.87 MASTECTOMY ## 4 brca_metabric MB-0006 MB-0006 47.68 MASTECTOMY ## 5 brca_metabric MB-0008 MB-0008 76.97 MASTECTOMY ## 6 brca_metabric MB-0010 MB-0010 78.77 MASTECTOMY

Basic ggplot ggplot(metabric, aes(x = type_of_breast_surgery, y = tumor_size)) + geom_boxplot() ## Warning: Removed 149 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range ## (stat_boxplot()).

Question English

I have shared with you an initial plot. As you can see, this plot is not yet publication-ready. Your task: Choose at least three modifications you think will improve the plot and make it more flexible and creative. You can select from the following examples or come up with your own ideas: Change the background/theme of the plot. Modify the X and Y axis titles. Use facet_wrap() or facet_grid() to separate categories. Change the color of the plot (using fill or color). Adjust labels, scales, legends, or text sizes. Other creative enhancements you think improve the visualization. Deliverable: Implement your chosen modifications in at least three different ways, and briefly explain why you made each choice. Español

Les he compartido un gráfico inicial que, como ven, no está listo para publicación.

Su tarea:

Elijan al menos tres modificaciones que ustedes crean que mejorarán el gráfico y lo harán más flexible y creativo.

Pueden escoger entre los siguientes ejemplos o proponer sus propias ideas: Cambiar el fondo/tema del gráfico. Modificar los títulos de los ejes X y Y. Usar facet_wrap() o facet_grid() para separar categorías. Cambiar el color del gráfico (usando fill o color). justar etiquetas, escalas, leyendas o tamaños de texto. Otras mejoras creativas que consideren útiles. Entrega: Implementen sus modificaciones en al menos tres formas diferentes, y expliquen brevemente por qué hicieron cada cambio.

Reference

Curtis C, Shah SP, Chin SF, Turashvili G, Rueda OM, Dunning MJ, Speed D, Lynch AG, Samarajiwa S, Yuan Y, Gräf S, Ha G, Haffari G, Bashashati A, Russell R, McKinney S; METABRIC Group; Langerød A, Green A, Provenzano E, Wishart G, Pinder S, Watson P, Markowetz F, Murphy L, Ellis I, Purushotham A, Børresen-Dale AL, Brenton JD, Tavaré S, Caldas C, Aparicio S. The genomic and transcriptomic architecture of 2,000 breast tumours reveals novel subgroups. Nature. 2012 Apr 18;486(7403):346-52. doi: 10.1038/nature10983. PMID: 22522925; PMCID: PMC3440846.

metabric <- read.csv("brca_metabric_clinical_data.csv") %>%
  clean_names()
# Improved Plot 1: Changed theme and axis titles
ggplot(metabric, aes(x = type_of_breast_surgery,
                     y = tumor_size)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", color = "darkblue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Tumor Size by Type of Breast Surgery",
       x = "Type of Breast Surgery",
       y = "Tumor Size (mm)")
## Warning: Removed 149 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

# Improved Plot 2: Added facet_wrap by age group
metabric$age_group <- cut(metabric$age_at_diagnosis,
                          breaks = c(0, 40, 60, 80, 100),
                          labels = c("<40", "40-60", "60-80", "80
+"))
ggplot(metabric, aes(x = type_of_breast_surgery,
                     y = tumor_size)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen", color = "darkgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~ age_group) +
  theme_light() +
  labs(title = "Tumor Size by Type of Breast Surgery and Age Group",
       x = "Type of Breast Surgery",
       y = "Tumor Size (mm)")
## Warning: Removed 149 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

# Explanation: I added facet_wrap to separate the data by age groups, which allows for better comparison across different age categories.
# Improved Plot 3: Changed color scheme and adjusted text size
ggplot(metabric, aes(x = type_of_breast_surgery,
                     y = tumor_size)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = type_of_breast_surgery)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")) +
  labs(title = "Tumor Size by Type of Breast Surgery",
       x = "Type of Breast Surgery",
       y = "Tumor Size (mm)")
## Warning: Removed 149 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

# Explanation: I used a color palette to differentiate the boxplots better and adjusted the text size for improved readability.
